title: Corporation projects schemas and types do not match ESI's response shapes
description: Found converting corporation-projects.steps.ts to the transport seam. src/schemas/corporation-projects.ts expects bare arrays with project_id/start_time and contributor records with character_id/contribution. The generated OpenAPI types say: project list is {cursor, projects:[{id: string, name, progress:{current,desired}, state,...}]}; contributors are {contributors:[{contributed,id,name}], cursor}; a single contribution is {contributed, last_modified}. A real ESI response therefore fails validation and the client throws EsiValidationError. The feature file's Rules and the scenarios describe the wrong shapes too. Fix schema, hand-written types, client, Rules and fixtures together; the exported type change is breaking, so decide the SemVer impact.

title: [DES-08] Default all-pages call silently returns page 1 when a later page keeps failing
description: When a later page exhausts retries, the call-level retry re-requests page 1, gets a 304, and returns page 1 only with no error. Reproduced with mocked fetch at default 3 retries. Surface as PAGINATION_INCOMPLETE instead. Found while writing guides/PAGINATION.md.

title: [DES-08] Authenticated paginated results cached under unhashed key; repeat calls return page 1 only
description: paginationOrchestration.ts:79 calls cacheResponse without requiresAuth, so the combined multi-page body is stored under the raw URL while lookups use the token-hashed key (which holds only page 1). Repeat calls inside the TTL return page 1. Fix: pass requiresAuth; add an EARS rule under tests/bdd/features/core/pagination. Found while writing guides/PAGINATION.md.

title: [Phase 1] Make the BDD specification load-bearing

Establish queueResponse/withCachedEntry helpers, add an ESLint restricted-syntax ratchet over the 43 offending step files, convert domain by domain starting with the request pipeline, measure with a BDD-only Stryker run, and fix the performance feature so latency Rules time the real parsing path.
acceptance_criteria: spyOn baseline empty; BDD-only mutation score reported and ratcheted per directory; every 5xx and optional-field Rule reconciled with the schema
notes: PR from feat/ramp-up-phases: seam + lint ratchet (0 violations), all step files converted, perf Rules time the real pipeline, BDD-only Stryker + per-directory ratchet nightly. Remaining for exit: first nightly result to seed mutation-bdd-thresholds.json.

title: [Phase 0] Close the spec-audit holes
description:
scripts/spec-audit.ts has five gaps that let a non-compliant spec pass, which manufactures confidence:

1. The unconverted exception list can grow silently - additions are skipped, not failed.
2. Exception entries for deleted feature files never go stale.
3. A Feature with zero Rule blocks passes the audit.
4. The EARS If pattern does not enforce a non-empty condition followed by a comma before then.
5. tests/bdd/README.md claims step-body rules are audited when only feature ASTs are parsed.

Also: each check needs a negative fixture so the audit itself is tested.
acceptance_criteria: spec-audit self-tests green (one failing fixture per check); tests/bdd/README.md lists exactly the checks the script performs; npm run spec:audit still passes on the real feature tree

title: [epic] Hermes-grade ramp-up: load-bearing spec, pipeline and agent hardening
description:
Adopt the practices from the Hermes report where ESI.ts is behind, without regressing the areas where it is ahead (coverage, mutation, fuzz, supply chain). Plan artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/2FyDsDRf7ihFqiZ7ifQsmd

Core finding: ESI.ts has excellent code verification and a specification that is honest but not load-bearing - 437 of 438 BDD mock sites spy on the client's own public methods, so ~351 of 401 scenarios cannot fail for any bug in src/.

Phases 0-6 are filed as children of this epic.

title: Stale-on-error never serves for endpoints with a spec cache TTL
description: Found by Phase 3 while writing the stale-on-error Rules. The ETag cache entry for an endpoint with a spec TTL expires at the same moment the TTL cache hit stops being served, so a later 5xx finds no entry and rejects. Confirmed: GET status answered 503 after 31s rejected instead of serving stale. Either keep entries past their freshness TTL for revalidation/stale use, or document that stale-on-error applies only within the TTL window.

title: Unit client suites time out under jest --randomize: shared 429 test blocks the rate-limit group for 60s
description: Found by the Phase 4 nightly no-retry work. With jest --randomize, 80 tests across 20 tests/tdd client suites time out: each suite's shared HTTP 429 error test blocks the rate-limit group for 60s on the suite's shared client, so tests ordered after it hang. Normal order hides it because the 429 test runs last. Fix the shared helper to use a fresh client or reset the limiter, then enable --randomize in nightly-no-retry.yml.

title: [GATE/REL-02] Align CI with charter gate matrix: release gate, never-run validators, dead docs job, freshness diff

Generated-freshness diff omits scopes and rate-limit group files (ARCH-01). validate:auth-scopes only fails one direction of DES-04. example:sde-cross-ref points at a missing file (see esi-x3z). Either fix CI or correct the charter matrix. See guides/QUALITY-GATES.md.

title: [SEC-02/ARCH-09] Log lines carry unsanitised URLs; several call sites bypass the per-client logger
description: Only errors go through sanitizeUrl; pipeline log lines and the url context field carry raw URLs (post-interceptor). Rate limiter, batch helpers and ETag cache startup log with a null client; EsiTokenManager captures the global logger at construction so setLogger() later does not reach it. EsiClientConfig.logLevel JSDoc omits fatal; silent works but is not in LogLevel. See guides/LOGGING.md.

title: [ARCH-07] Error type fidelity: validation errors retryable, network faults untyped, safe mode and token refresh collapse types, [CODE] errors unsanitised
description: EsiValidationError has statusCode 0 so .retryable/isRetryable/isTimeout are true; non-timeout network failures are plain [ESIJS_ERROR] and never retried; withSafeMode maps CircuitOpenError and [CODE] errors to EsiError(0); TokenRevokedError/SsoError from the refresh callback surface as [TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED]; PAGINATION_INCOMPLETE puts the raw URL in its message; double prefixes like [ESIJS_ERROR] [NO_AUTH_TOKEN]. Complements esi-gyh. See guides/ERRORS.md.
notes: Network failures and DOMException aborts now surface as EsiError(0)/TimeoutError (commit on feat/ramp-up-phases). Remaining: validation errors retryable via status 0, safe-mode/token-refresh type collapse, unsanitised [CODE] messages, double prefixes.

title: Mutations returning 201/204 do not invalidate the cache path prefix
description: Status handling returns early for 201/204 before cacheResponse's non-GET invalidation runs, so POST/PUT/DELETE that return 201/204 leave stale cached GETs. Found while writing guides/ARCHITECTURE.md.
close_reason: Fixed on feat/ramp-up-phases: invalidateAfterWrite runs for 201/204

title: stream*/fetchAll* throw EsiError 304 after a normal call to the same endpoint
description: stream*/fetchAll* bypass response interceptors, spec-TTL cache and dedup but still send If-None-Match from the ETag cache, so a 304 with no usable body throws. Found while writing guides/PAGINATION.md and ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: TestDataFactory builders produce payloads the Zod schemas reject

Step files now work around these locally. Fix the builders to emit schema-valid, ESI-realistic payloads and drop the local workarounds.
